content: Triamcinolone is a medication prescribed to alleviate symptoms such as itching, redness, dryness, crusting, scaling, inflammation, and discomfort associated with various skin conditions. It is also used to relieve the discomfort caused by mouth sores. In some cases, it may be prescribed for other uses; consult your doctor or pharmacist for additional information. Triamcinolone is available in different forms, including ointment, cream, lotion, liquid, aerosol (spray) for skin application, and paste for use in the mouth. Typically, it is applied two to four times daily. For mouth sores, it is applied at bedtime and, if necessary, two or three times daily, preferably after meals. Follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully, and consult your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Use triamcinolone exactly as directed. Do not use more or less of it or apply it more frequently than prescribed. Avoid applying it to other areas of your body or wrapping/bandaging the treated area unless instructed by your doctor. Before applying the medication, thoroughly wash or soak the affected area unless doing so irritates your skin. Apply the ointment, cream, liquid, or lotion sparingly in a thin film and gently rub it in. For scalp application, part your hair, apply a small amount of the medication to the affected area, and rub it in gently. Protect the area from washing or rubbing until the medication dries. You may wash your hair as usual but not immediately after applying the medication. When using an aerosol, shake the container well and spray the affected area from a distance of 3 to 6 inches for about 2 seconds to cover an area the size of your hand. Avoid inhaling the vapors, and if spraying near your face, cover your eyes. For mouth sores, press a small amount of paste onto the sore without rubbing until a thin film forms. Use more paste if the sore is large. If the sore does not begin to heal within 7 days, contact your doctor. Avoid prolonged use of triamcinolone on the face, genital or rectal areas, skin creases, or armpits unless directed by your doctor. If using it on your face, keep it away from your eyes. Do not apply cosmetics or other skin preparations to the treated area without consulting your doctor. If using triamcinolone on a child’s diaper area, avoid tight-fitting diapers or plastic pants, as this may increase side effects. If your doctor instructs you to wrap or bandage the treated area, follow these steps: Soak or wash the area thoroughly. While the skin is moist, gently rub the medication into the affected areas. Cover the area with plastic wrap (e.g., Saran Wrap or Handi-Wrap). Secure the plastic with gauze, an elastic bandage, or adhesive tape on the normal skin adjacent to the treated area. Alternatively, use plastic gloves for hands, plastic bags for feet, or a shower cap for the scalp. Seal the edges of the plastic wrap carefully to ensure it adheres closely to the skin. If the area is moist, leave the edges partly unsealed or puncture the wrap to allow excess moisture to escape. Leave the plastic wrap in place as directed by your doctor, usually no more than 12 hours daily. Cleanse the skin and reapply the medication each time a new plastic wrapping is applied. Do not discontinue treatment abruptly without consulting your doctor. Before using triamcinolone, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to triamcinolone or any other drugs. Provide a list of all prescription and nonprescription medications you are taking, especially cancer chemotherapy agents, other topical medications, and vitamins. Notify your doctor if you have an infection or a history of diabetes, glaucoma, cataracts, circulation disorders, or immune disorders. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, inform your doctor. If you become pregnant while using triamcinolone, contact your doctor immediately. If you forget a dose, apply it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for the next dose, skip the missed dose and continue your regular dosing schedule. Do not apply a double dose to make up for a missed one. Although side effects from triamcinolone are uncommon, they can occur. Notify your doctor if you experience any of the following minor side effects, especially if they are severe or persistent: Drying or cracking of the skin Acne Itching Burning Changes in skin color If you experience any of the following severe side effects, contact your doctor immediately: Severe skin rash Difficulty breathing or swallowing Wheezing Skin infection (redness, swelling, or oozing of pus) If you experience a serious side effect, you or your doctor may report it to the FDA’s MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program online or by phone. Store this medication in its original container, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Follow the storage instructions on the package. Dispose of any outdated or unused medication properly. Do not use it to treat other skin conditions. Consult your pharmacist about the proper disposal of medications. Keep all appointments with your doctor. Do not share your medication with others. If you have questions about refilling your prescription, ask your pharmacist.
